name: Billy Graham
life_summary: Billy Graham was born in 1918 and grew up on a dairy farm in Charlotte, North Carolina. In November 1934, aged 15, he committed his life to Christ at a revival led by Mordecai Ham. After a semester at Bob Jones College he studied at the Florida Bible Institute (1937–40), where Peniel Baptist Church in Palatka ordained him in 1939, and then at Wheaton College, graduating in June 1943 and marrying Ruth Bell that August. After pastoring the Village Church of Western Springs, Illinois (1943–45), he became Youth for Christ's first full-time evangelist, and from 1948 to 1952 he was president of Northwestern Schools in Minneapolis. His 1949 Los Angeles campaign brought him national attention, and in 1950 the Billy Graham Evangelistic Association (BGEA) was incorporated; it organised his crusades, including London (1954) and New York (1957), and his broadcasts. From 1977 he also preached in communist Eastern Europe, spoke in Moscow in 1982, visited China in 1988 and North Korea in 1992 and 1994, and he was honorary chairman of the 1974 Lausanne Congress. After Parkinson's disease was announced in 1992, his son Franklin took over the BGEA in 2000–01, and after a last crusade in New York in 2005 Graham lived in retirement at Montreat, where Ruth died in 2007 and he died in 2018, aged 99.

phases.label: Bible college and Wheaton
phases.summary: He spent one semester at Bob Jones College in autumn 1936, then from early 1937 studied at the Florida Bible Institute in Temple Terrace near Tampa, where he began preaching, was ordained by Peniel Baptist Church, Palatka, in 1939 and graduated in 1940. At Wheaton College (1940–43) he majored in anthropology and was pastor of the United Gospel Tabernacle while a student.

phases.label: Western Springs and Youth for Christ
phases.summary: Newly married, he was pastor of the Village Church of Western Springs, Illinois (1943–45), then in January 1945 left to become Youth for Christ's first full-time evangelist. In 1945 the family moved to Montreat, North Carolina, where daughters Gigi (1945) and Anne (1948) were born; in December 1947 W. B. Riley chose him to lead Northwestern Schools, Minneapolis, which he did from 1948.
phases.place: Western Springs, Illinois; Montreat, North Carolina; Minneapolis, Minnesota

phases.label: Breakthrough crusades, BGEA founding
phases.summary: His extended 1949 Los Angeles campaign made him nationally known, and in 1950 the BGEA was incorporated in Minnesota and the Hour of Decision broadcast began. He remained president of Northwestern until 1952 and led long crusades in Chattanooga (1953), London (1954) and New York (1957); daughter Ruth (1950) and son Franklin (1952) were born.
phases.place: Montreat, North Carolina; Minneapolis; Los Angeles; London; New York

phases.label: Worldwide crusade ministry
phases.summary: With Montreat as home, he held crusades around the world, including Seoul in 1973, and was honorary chairman of the 1974 Lausanne Congress. From 1977 he preached in communist Eastern Europe, spoke at a Moscow peace conference in 1982 and visited China in 1988; his youngest son, Ned, was born in 1958.

phases.label: Final crusades and succession
phases.summary: After his Parkinson's disease was announced in 1992 he kept preaching, visited North Korea in 1992 and 1994, handed BGEA leadership to Franklin in 2000–01, and spoke at the 2001 National Cathedral service. He held his final crusade in New York in June 2005.

phases.label: Retirement at Montreat
phases.summary: In retirement at Montreat he made a few appearances, including New Orleans in March 2006. The Billy Graham Library in Charlotte was dedicated in May 2007, weeks before Ruth died that June; he gave a last televised message in 2013 and died at home in 2018.

corrections: Changed 'dairy farm near Charlotte' to 'dairy farm in Charlotte', following the BGEA biography's wording.
Added an event for his arrival at the Florida Bible Institute in late January 1937 (Billy Graham Library, quoting his autobiography) to support the 1937 start date.

United Gospel Tabernacle event: sources disagree (BGEA says 1941, BGEA Canada says spring 1941, Wheaton archives say September 1941), so the date is now '1941' and the Wheaton dates are credited to Wheaton's archives.
Youth for Christ event dated January 1945 (BGEA Canada, Ruth Bell Graham Part 2) instead of just 1945; dropped the Billy Graham Library YFC page as a source because it gives no date.
Montreat move: changed from 'September 1945' to '1945'. The source says only that the move came just before Gigi's birth in September 1945, not that the move was in September.
Northwestern: made clear that Riley chose him in December 1947 and that he served as president from 1948 to 1952 (University of Northwestern).
Removed the BGEA Media biography as a source for the 1950 BGEA/Hour of Decision event; the facts rest on the BGEA Ministry Timeline.
New York 1957: said ABC's live broadcasts began in June, per the BGEA timeline.
Added a 1977 Hungary event (Official Obituary; Christianity Today) to support the start of his Eastern Bloc ministry.
Moscow 1982 event narrowed from 'May 1982' to 11 May 1982, the date of his address according to Christianity Today; noted that the remark was as reported.

Parkinson's event reworded: his spokesman announced it in July 1992 and said symptoms had been present for three years (full Tampa Bay Times text checked). Hydrocephalus claim moved out of this event.
2005 final crusade: removed the unsupported 'preached from a seated pulpit' claim; kept age 86 and the walker, and added Parkinson's and prostate cancer from ABC News.
Ruth's death event: added the place (their home in Montreat) and a Christianity Today 2007 source, because the memorial pages do not say where she died.
Life summary: replaced 'preached in ... the Soviet Union' with 'spoke in Moscow in 1982' and dated the China and North Korea visits. No source confirmed a preaching tour of the USSR.
Life summary: 'helped bring about the Lausanne Congress' now reads 'honorary chairman', per the Wheaton archives; added the 1992 Parkinson's announcement.
Phase 1936–1943: added the Florida Bible Institute graduation (1940) and the Library FBI source; the Tabernacle pastorate is no longer dated 'from 1941'.
Phase 1949–1957: added the Chattanooga 1953 crusade. Phase 1957–1990: reworded the communist-country ministry the same way as the life summary.
Phase 1990–2005: 'reported' changed to 'announced' and the Tampa Bay Times source added. Phase 2005–2018: New Orleans dated March 2006 and the Library dedication dated May 2007 (Memorial Biography).
